title: Adaptive Threshold Autoscaler with Quantile Targeting
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Current autoscaling policies rely on single-point metrics (avg latency or per-GPU utilization) which either under-provision for tail latency or cause oscillation and cost spikes. Proposal: Implement an Adaptive Threshold Autoscaler (ATA) that targets quantile latency objectives (p50, p95, p99) in combination with throughput-per-GPU targets. ATA uses a two-layer decision model: (1) short-term reactive adjustments based on observed quantiles and queue depth, and (2) medium-term proactive adjustments using short workload forecasts (10–60s) derived from recent request arrival rate. Safety controls include hard min/max node limits, cooldown windows, dampening (minimum scale step intervals), and an emergency burst floor to absorb transient spikes without immediate scale-out. The controller will expose per-fleet policy knobs (quantile targets, throughput floor, max parallel scale, cost cap) and a diagnostic trace for every scale decision to aid postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: Controller scales up/down to meet configured p95 latency target within configured SLO window on synthetic workload tests
No >3x oscillation in node count for steady traffic patterns over 15 minutes in chaos tests
Safety limits (min/max nodes, cooldown) prevent unbounded scale and protect cost cap in load tests
Feature gated rollout enabled with canary per-region and metrics surfaced in Console (per-route p50/p95/p99, decisions, prediction error)
